pr_body:
Fix #55957. 

The `bt_buf_get_evt` test was using `net_buf` structures without allocating it properly.

issue_context.title: bluetooth.host.bt_buf_get_evt tests fail with host GCC 11
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `bluetooth.host.bt_buf_get_evt` tests fail when building with the host GCC 11.3.

Note that these tests succeed when building with the host GCC 9.3, which is the default GCC version in Ubuntu 20.04 and currently used in the main CI.

**To Reproduce**

```
scripts/twister -v -N -p unit_testing -s tests/bluetooth/host/buf/bt_buf_get_evt/bluetooth.host.bt_buf_get_evt.hci_acl_flow_control
```

**Expected behavior**

Test passes.

**Impact**

review_comments: how does this work? you're casting a size 1 array to a struct net_buf (with much more than 1 byte).
I think I made a mistake. `expected_buf_data` should be `sizeof(struct net_buf) + user_data_size`.
